status: Proposed (2026-10-07) for the owner: 'the textures on the console man, they need to be full on custom details, youre using generic textures on them which looks pretty bad' and 'basically everything using the metal tile grid needs to get replaced with custom textures'. Read by tools/blender/hs_kit.py when a prop set builds (build_bridge_props.py, build_machinery_props.py, build_suite_props.py); the atlases it bakes are assets/models/<set>/atlas/<prop>.png. The colours, wear and light are first choices made by eye on the contact sheets, not decisions: the owner judges them.
_rules: Every prop carries a second UV map, the atlas (glTF TEXCOORD_1; TEXCOORD_0 stays the metre UVs): its faces cut into planar charts (connected triangles of one plane), each laid flat at one texel density, packed into one square with margin_px of padding round every chart, at the highest density up to max_px_per_m that fits. The square is atlas.px (256) unless that leaves the prop under min_px_per_m, when it doubles until it does not or reaches px_max: a 10 m reactor or a shuttle needs 1024 px to read at walking distance. The manifest records each prop's px and px_per_m.

The atlas is baked, never painted: a detail version of the prop that exists only for the bake (the low-poly surfaces plus details modelled on them: seams, bolts, vents, buttons, lamps, labels) is baked onto the atlas with Cycles, selected to active, rays from cage_m out along each face. bake_scale times the atlas's size, samples per pixel, fixed seed, no denoiser; area-averaged in linear light to atlas.px, encoded sRGB and reduced to atlas.colours colours as the panels are (tools/materials/postprocess.py), by max coverage rather than median cut, so a small saturated area (a lamp, a station's stripe) keeps its colour. A second bake of emission only is the alpha mask: 255 where it glows (lamps, LEDs, status displays), 0 elsewhere.

The light is the panels' look, per face: every face is lit by an ambient of bake.ambient and a key from bake.key_tangent in the face's own frame (x right, y up the face, z out of it; a top face's up runs away from the prop's front), scaled so an unoccluded flat face renders at exactly its colour, a detail's slope lighter or darker as it turns to the key or away (at most relief_max times its colour). Relief, occlusion (wear.crevice within crevice_m), grime, edge wear and, in working spaces, rust are baked in; there are no normal maps on the Pi 5.

roles maps a prop's material role to the finish its faces bake in; a builder may override it per prop (a desk's bulkhead faces in wood). screen faces bake flat and dark (a page draws the console faces on them); accent faces bake light and neutral (a page multiplies them by the station's colour); upholstery faces bake the upholstery layer images (assets/textures/panels/256) multiplied by the chair's tint (data/materials/panels.json upholstery.tints_srgb), so the atlas carries the colour.

A finish is a kind and colours (sRGB, 0-1): paint and metal (wear on edges), brushed (streaks along the face), hazard (stripes 0.125 m apart, colours srgb and srgb_b), flat (no edge wear: seams, wells, glass, stencils), glow (emissive: masked), layer (a panel layer image times a tint), wood, laminate and fabric. sets names the wear each prop set takes.
Units: metres (_m), pixels (_px), sRGB components 0-1 (_srgb, srgb), fractions 0-1. An unknown key or a missing one stops the build with its path.
